title: Memory & input limits
blurb: Stress-tests Android-only kTranslationAPI limits from Chromium source: the 256 KiB UTF-8 per-call input cap (QuotaExceededError), UTF-8 byte counting vs String.length on multi-byte scripts, lossless chunk planning, inputQuota/measureInputUsage(), and 1-minute idle model unload latency.
question: How do Android's 256 KiB UTF-8 per-call input cap and 1-minute idle model unload affect multi-byte text translation when inputQuota still reports Infinity?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux), the UTF-8 byte counter and lossless chunk planner verified 300 KiB splitting into 2 chunks and 120,000 Hindi characters measuring 302,072 UTF-8 bytes (over the 262,144-byte cap); live QuotaExceededError and 65 s idle unload timing require an installed pack on Chrome for Android 161 and were not verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux, byte counter and chunk planner verified); on-device QuotaExceededError and idle unload not verified on Chrome for Android 161

friction.summary: Android caps each translate() call at 256 KiB of UTF-8 bytes (QuotaExceededError), while inputQuota returns Infinity and measureInputUsage() resolves 0
friction.repro: Check translator.inputQuota and await translator.measureInputUsage(text) on Chrome (blink translator.cc returns Infinity and 0 on every platform), then pass >262,144 UTF-8 bytes on Android (for example 120,000 Devanagari characters = 302,072 bytes); Android rejects with QuotaExceededError.
friction.workaround: Measure payloads with TextEncoder().encode(text).byteLength rather than String.length or inputQuota, and chunk long text below 256 KiB (or smaller 8–64 KiB chunks) before calling translate().

friction.summary: Android unloads idle language pairs (~79–84 MiB each) after 1 minute, adding cold-reload latency to the next translate() call
friction.repro: Translate a sentence on Chrome for Android 161, leave the Translator instance idle for >60 seconds (TranslationAPIModelIdleUnloadTimeout = 1 minute), and time the next translate() call.
friction.workaround: Keep UI responsive during the first translation after idle periods with an explicit pending indicator rather than assuming uniform warm latency.
